market.title: When AI models refuse to fight hackers
market.summary: In the race to fend off AI-enabled cyber threats , security teams are confronting a new problem: The AI models they rely on to investigate attacks can suddenly refuse to help. Why it matters: While AI giants race to build AI tools that can respond quickly to hacking or other malicious online threats, strict guardrails on their most powerful models lock out defenders mid-investigation, leaving them scrambling for alternatives at critical moments. What's happening: OpenCode, an open-source AI coding agent, said it was compromised over the weekend, allowing attackers to obtain API keys belonging to some customers, including keys for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google services. OpenCode said the breach was "related to a large scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users." OpenCode co-creator Dax Raad said attackers had been targeting its systems continuously for 48 hours, forcing the company to keep its own AI agents running around the clock to respond. OpenAI , Google and Anthropic have said they worked with affected customers to revoke exposed API keys and address unauthorized usage charges. Zoom in: Raad said on X that frontier AI models initially helped investigate the breach but then "started refusing." The models' safety restrictions reportedly began blocking requests as the investigation turned to potentially malicious code, even though OpenCode was trying to defend its own systems. OpenCode then gained access to OpenAI's Daybreak Blue program, which gives vetted cybersecurity defenders access to models with fewer restrictions. "We definitely need to be more proactive and we've made so many improvements over the last few days," Raad wrote on X Monday. The big picture: The incident underscored a dilemma facing cybersecurity teams trying to figure out when to use powerful proprietary AI models, which come with built-in restrictions, or open-weight alternatives that offer greater control over how they're deployed. When Hugging Face discovered suspicious activity on its systems that it later linked to OpenAI's own agents, its security team turned to a Chinese open-weight model to help investigate after encountering restrictions on frontier models. Yes, but: AI companies maintain that they need to gate access to their most powerful models to ensure that malicious actors can't abuse their cyber capabilities. Between the lines: Cybersecurity teams will have to figure out how to balance the need for faster AI-powered defenses with restrictions designed to keep those same capabilities out of attackers' hands, Chris Jones, chief technology officer at Nightwing, told Axios. "We're all going to have to figure out how that race gets modulated over time," Jones said. "That's a big piece here." Go deeper : Anthropic and OpenAI are now cybersecurity's kingmakers

ALT.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis Clinical Trial and Competitive Landscape Expands as 180+ Companies Target New Treatment Options | DelveInsight
ALT.summary: The MASH (Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis) market is rapidly expanding with over 180 companies developing 200+ pipeline therapies. Two drugs have been approved: REZDIFFRA (resmetirom) by Madrigal Pharmaceuticals and LIPAGLYN/BILYPSA (saroglitazar magnesium) by Zydus Lifesciences. The competitive landscape is intensifying with emerging mechanisms of action including FGF21 replacements, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and dual glucagon/GLP-1 agonists, with approximately 5+ drugs in late-stage development and 100+ in mid and early stages.

GUTS.title: Pomerantz Law Firm Announces the Filing of a Class Action Against Fractyl Health, Inc. and Certain Officers – GUTS
GUTS.summary: Pomerantz LLP has filed a class action lawsuit against Fractyl Health, Inc. (NASDAQ: GUTS) and certain officers for alleged securities fraud. The lawsuit claims Defendants made materially false and misleading statements about the efficacy of Revita, their metabolic therapy device, while conducting public offerings in August-September 2025. On January 29, 2026, Fractyl disclosed disappointing six-month data from the REMAIN-1 Midpoint Cohort showing only 4.5% weight regain versus 7.5% in the sham arm, significantly below expectations. The disclosure revealed operational issues at one clinical site compromised study integrity. Following the announcement, Fractyl's stock price plummeted 68.03% on January 29, 2026, and fell an additional 21.37% on January 30, 2026.

High fuel costs from Middle East tensions, escalated labor and airport costs, and high debt levels are pressuring profitability, though solid bookings and network optimization support revenue growth.

KEX.title: JetBlue Gears Up for Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
KEX.summary: JetBlue Airways is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 27 with expectations for a loss of 52 cents per share, wider than previous estimates. The airline faces significant headwinds from elevated fuel costs ($3.49/gallon expected), non-fuel expense pressures with CASM ex-fuel growth of 2.5-4.5%, operational disruptions, and a substantial $8.48 billion debt burden. The company's negative Earnings ESP of -6.22% and Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) suggest limited likelihood of beating consensus estimates.

ODFL.title: Union Pacific Gears Up to Report Q3 Earnings: Is a Beat in Store?
ODFL.summary: Union Pacific (UNP) is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $3.47 per share (up 12.7% YoY) with revenues projected at $7.12 billion (up 14% YoY), driven by freight revenue growth of 14.8%. However, lower shipment volumes, Middle East tensions, and supply-chain disruptions may pressure results. The company has a positive earnings surprise history and an Earnings ESP of +0.28% with a Zacks Rank #3.

HTLD.title: Heartland Express (HTLD) Reports Q3 Earnings: What Key Metrics Have to Say
HTLD.summary: Heartland Express reported Q3 2026 revenue of $179.5 million, down 8.7% year-over-year and missing the consensus estimate of $188.77 million by 4.91%. EPS came in at $0.01 versus consensus of $0.02, representing a 50% miss. The company's operating ratio was 98.7%, slightly worse than the 98.1% estimate. Operating revenue excluding fuel surcharge declined 14.9% year-over-year. The stock has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and has underperformed the S&P 500 by 10.2% over the past month.

SFST.title: Compared to Estimates, Southern First (SFST) Q3 Earnings: A Look at Key Metrics
SFST.summary: Southern First reported Q3 2026 revenue of $37.53 million, up 20.6% year-over-year, slightly missing consensus estimates by 0.04%. EPS of $1.28 beat expectations by 1.59%. Key metrics showed mixed results: efficiency ratio matched estimates at 54.1%, net interest margin exceeded expectations at 3% vs 2.9% estimated, but noninterest income fell short at $2.86M vs $3.57M estimated. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and has underperformed the broader market, declining 3.4% over the past month.

AZN.title: GSK's New Drugs and Pipeline Hold the Key to Long-Term Growth
AZN.summary: GSK is focusing on newer specialty medicines and vaccines to offset pressure from older products and drive long-term growth. TOT.title: Eni Advances Coral North, Evaluates Third Mozambique LNG Facility

CDNL.title: Cardinal Infrastructure Group Investigated by the Portnoy Law Firm

The stock subsequently fell more than 36%.

FSM.title: Fortuna intersects 0.96 g/t gold over 350 meters at the Lindero Mine, Argentina
FSM.summary: Fortuna Mining Corp. announced positive results from its 2026 infill drilling program at the Lindero gold porphyry deposit in Argentina. The drilling confirmed gold mineralization extends significantly below the current life-of-mine pit design, with multiple intersections showing gold grades consistent with or higher than block model estimates. The company plans to incorporate these results into an updated block model and pit design by year-end, supporting a revised life-of-mine plan and updated mineral reserve estimate for release in Q1 2027.

ADRZY.title: Flue Gas Desulfurization (FGD) System Market: Global Forecast to 2031 | Tougher Sulfur Rules Keep Flue-Gas Scrubbers in Demand as Energy Transition Looms
ADRZY.summary: The global flue gas desulfurization system market is projected to grow from $23.6 billion in 2026 to $31.7 billion by 2031, with a CAGR of 6.1%. Growth is driven by stringent SO2 emission regulations, retrofit programs for aging coal plants, and continued coal reliance in developing economies. Dry & semi-dry FGD systems are expected to record the highest growth, while power generation remains the leading end-use industry. Europe is positioned as the second-largest regional market.

SBGSY.title: Water shortages will threaten growth within five years, say over half of European industrial leaders
SBGSY.summary: A new Schneider Electric report reveals water stress now ranks among the top business continuity risks for European industrial companies, alongside cyber-attacks and supply chain disruption. Despite 86% of industrial leaders believing smart water technology can reduce costs, only 42% have deployed digital twins and similar solutions. The research highlights a significant gap between awareness and adoption of water management technologies, with 47% of companies already increasing water efficiency investments.

XBIT.title: XBiotech annonce des résultats d’efficacité finaux positifs de phase II pour l’essai TASKIN commandité par un chercheur dans le cancer colorectal métastatique réfractaire
XBIT.summary: XBiotech announced positive Phase II results for its anti-IL-1α monoclonal antibody vilamakitug (Natrunix) in treating refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. ANAB.title: Jemperli (dostarlimab) Approved in the U.S. as First and Only Immunotherapy for Adults with MSI-H/dMMR Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
ANAB.summary: GSK received FDA approval for Jemperli (dostarlimab) as the first immunotherapy for adults with stage II and III MSI-H/dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer. The AZUR-1 trial showed 68% of patients achieved sustained clinical complete responses at 12 months without surgery, with no disease recurrences reported among responders after median follow-up of over 2 years. The approval could help eligible patients avoid chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery.

ARDX.title: Robbins LLP Urges ARDX Stockholders to Contact the Firm for Information About the Securities Class Action Against Ardelyx, Inc.
ARDX.summary: A securities class action has been filed against Ardelyx, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARDX) alleging the company misled investors about its commercial performance and growth prospects for its drug products IBSRELA and XPHOZAH. The lawsuit covers purchases between January 13, 2025 and August 6, 2026. On August 6, 2026, Ardelyx reduced its full-year 2026 IBSRELA revenue guidance and withdrew long-term XPHOZAH guidance due to increased payer access barriers, causing the stock to drop 18% in one day from $4.87 to $4.00 per share.

FTK.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Flotek Industries, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
FTK.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Flotek Industries, Inc. (NYSE: FTK) alleging that company executives made materially false and misleading statements regarding a PREPA power generation project contract. The complaint claims defendants failed to disclose credible doubts about the consortium parties' experience and financial capacity, putting revenue realization at risk. Investors who purchased Flotek securities between August 3-17, 2026 are encouraged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 26, 2026.

RSG.title: 2 Industries Beyond AI With Long-Term Demand Drivers for 2027
RSG.summary: As AI dominates investment focus, healthcare and waste management sectors offer alternative diversification opportunities. Healthcare benefits from an aging population and rising medical needs, while waste management provides recurring revenue from essential services. Key companies like Abbott, Johnson & Johnson, Stryker, Waste Management, and Republic Services are positioned to capitalize on these structural trends.

SYK.title: Stryker Enters Soft-Tissue Robotics With $400 Million CMR Deal
SYK.summary: Stryker announced a $400 million preferred equity investment in CMR Surgical, gaining exclusive U.S. sales rights for the Versius robotic surgery platform and an option to acquire the company. The deal allows Stryker to expand into soft-tissue robotics, complementing its existing Mako orthopedic platform, while CMR Surgical retains global commercialization rights outside the U.S.

Investors who suffered losses have until November 30, 2026 to request lead plaintiff status.

MEMI.title: Miracles Surpasses 100,000 Personalized Children's Books, Now Printed in the USA for American Families
MEMI.summary: Miracles, a personalized children's book company, announced it has printed over 100,000 books for more than 45,000 families. Each book features a child as the hero in 14 illustrated scenes, with a free preview available before purchase starting at $34.99.

MEMI.title: Miracles knackt die Marke von 100.000 personalisierten Kinderbüchern
